prerequisites: Having studied Physics in 2nd year of Bachillerato (high school)
Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and differentiation and integration of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of wave and know its mathematical characterization as well as basic wave phenomena.
Know the basic concepts and laws of electromagnetism and apply them to the analysis of simple electromagnetic situations in vacuum and in material media.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and put into practice problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Electrostatics: Electric charge, Coulomb's Law, Electrostatic field and potential, Charge distributions, Electric dipole, Gauss's Law, Conductors, Capacitors, Electric field energy, Dielectrics.
Electric Current: Intensity and density of electric current, Ohm's Law, Resistance, Joule effect, Generators: Electromotive force, DC circuits.

Magnetostatics: Magnetic field, Lorentz Law: Magnetic induction, Hall effect, Magnetic force on an electric current, Magnetic moment on a loop, Biot-Savart Law, Force between currents, Ampere's Theorem, Magnetic field energy, Magnetism in matter.
Time-varying electromagnetic fields: Electromagnetic induction: Faraday-Henry Law, Self-induction, Maxwell's Equations, RLC circuits, Electrical oscillations.
Oscillations: Free oscillations, Damped oscillations, Forced oscillations.
Waves: Generalities. Mechanical waves: Concept of wave, Wave differential equation, Classification of waves, Harmonic waves, Mechanical waves, Wave phenomena, Doppler effect.
Practical 2. Capacitor Charging / Magnetic Field of a Solenoid.
Practical 4. Mechanical Waves / Standing Waves on a String.
teaching_methods: Exposition and explanation of theoretical contents by the professor
Examples of course content and solving typical problems by the professor
Exposition and defense of problems, assignments, projects
Use of simulation software and/or experimental data processing
Analysis of results and preparation of practice reports
Evaluation activities in very small groups
Study of theoretical-practical contents presented in class and laboratory by the professor
Solving problems and preparing practice reports, assignments, etc. proposed by the professor for individual or group work
Use of the University of Oviedo's virtual platform

assessment_methods.method: Examén Teórico (ET) (if T1 minimum not met)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if minimums for Partial Exam (T1) and Partial Exam (T2) are met, the theory grade is (0.35 x T1) + (0.40 x T2) + (0.10 x PA). If the T1 minimum is not met, the theory grade is (0.75 x ET) + (0.10 x PA). Practical work (P1) and Practical Exam (P2) contribute to the practical grade, which is (0.08 x P1) + (0.07 x P2), provided 75% attendance to practical sessions is met. The final grade is the sum of Theory and Practical grades, but if minimums or attendance are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, the theory grade is (0.75 x ET) + (0.10 x PA), and the practical grade is maintained if 75% attendance is met, otherwise, it is (0.15 x P2) from a new practical exam. In cases of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, students may be requested to defend their work orally.
